items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: You see on piano we had Louis Russell on piano... Louis Russell, what did I tell you, that piano player died, he recommended me to Jell-A-Roll-Martin.

ctx.x: Well I'll give you a few of them. You see on piano we had Louis Russell on piano, and banjo, Willie Foster, that's Pop Foster's brother, on banjo. On drums we had Paul Barbaran on drums. And on bass we had a bass player called Buford. Now on trumpet we had King Oliver, Red Island, so far back I can't think of the boy's name. Yeah. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I remember. That's what I…
Great kind of guy. Darnell Harris?

items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: I recorded, it's a record I recorded with Louis Russell's band.

ctx.x: You went on to New York band with them? With that section.

And on the percussion we had on piano, Louis Russell and Paul Barbaran on drums. But the band didn't have any success. We stayed there and we worked at the Savoy Ballroom. We had no more than about two weeks and whatever came up, King Oliver came out. He didn't seem, he could get enough money. So he had offered to go to the cotton club and that was his great mistake. He wouldn't accept it. And that was King Oliver's downfall. Because he didn't think there was enough money in it and he wouldn't accept it. So Duke…
That's when Barney went with him.

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: when you joined the band... Louis Russell did all of that... we had Kid O'Reilly on trombone, but Louis Russell did all of that.

ctx.x: Who would do the telling then, I mean, when you joined the band, who would really rock the band?
Well, Louis Russell, Louis Russell did all of that.
Was he doing a range here in the band? Was he doing a range here?
